Then came the night when the physical and mental torture was so hellish I feared I would burst through my window, sash and all. Somehow I managed to drag my mattress to a lower floor, lest I suddenly leap. A doctor came with a heavy Saturday. Next they found me drinking both Gin and Saturday. This combination soon landed me on the rocks. People feared for my sanity. So did I. I could eat little or nothing when drinking and I was £40 underweight. Now we see a dye who's dying from malnutrition. These calories that he's getting are from the alcohol. They are empty calories. None of the things necessary for life, and slowly, slowly, slowly, he's beginning to die now from malnutrition. Without some help from other sources and other people, Bill probably wouldn't have lasted much longer. Next paragraph, he said my brother-in-law is a fellow named Doctor Leonard Strong, married to Bill's sister. My brother-in-law as a physician and through his kindness and that of my mother, I was placed in an actually known hospital for the mental and physical rehabilitation of Alcoholics, the town's hospital. New York City the summer of 1933. Under the so-called belladonna treatment, my brain cleared. Belladonna was a drug that they used for withdrawal purposes. Today they use Valium and various other things. In those days it was called belladonna. Hydrotherapy and mild exercise help much hydrotherapy deals with the water treatment. chapters.content:
Chapter 65 How it Works Part 3

You can't really do much about a problem unless you understand the problem. And I found it was very difficult for me to even think about getting rid of self will because I didn't know where self-will came from. And thank God that Bill explained it to us in the 12:00 and 12:00. You know, I think we've all got to recognize the fact that Bill Wilson, when he wrote the big book, had only been sober a little over three years. He was not a great spiritual giant. He was not a great student of human nature. He was a night school lawyer and a New York City stock speculator. Yet he was able to write one of the most spiritual books dealing with human nature of the world has ever seen. When he wrote the big book, Alcoholics Anonymous, he did the absolute best that he could. Surely, surely God used Bill’s hand to write the big book. I don't think Bill could have done it by himself. 12 or 13 years later, though. Billy studied with some of the best minds in the world regarding spirituality. Bill had worked with many, many Alcoholics. He understood a lot more about spirituality and human nature in 195051 and 52 than he knew back in 1939. And I think he had some more information that he wanted to give to us. So that we would better be able to work the steps according to the big book Alcoholics Anonymous. And he wrote the 12:00 and 12:00. And one of the great mistakes we see people today doing, they're trying to work the steps out of the 12:00 and 12:00. But you can't work the steps out of the 12:00 and 12:00 because there's no directions on how to work them. He said that it's a series of essays. Designed to give us more information. So that we can better work the steps according to the big book Alcoholics Anonymous. On step four, in the 12 and 12. In a matter of about two or three pages. He taught me more about what makes me tick. What makes me think the way I think and act the way I act than I had ever learned before in 40 some odd years of living. And when I saw that and can really understand it. Then I can really begin to see why it's necessary for making to make this decision to turn my will and my life over the care of God as I understand. And we're going to put a little picture up here for. Just a few minutes. You got one of them in your book to match it. We're going to borrow just a little of that information out of the 12:00 and 12:00, and I think it'll make it a lot easier on us in step three and certainly it's going to lay the groundwork for us when we get to step forward. So let's look at this for just a few minutes. In the first couple of pages on step four in the 12 and 12. He talks about the three basic instincts of life. Which create this thing called self-will. He talks about the social Interstate, the security and state. And the sex instinct. And he said all human beings are born with these separate instincts as a part of their makeup and say if we didn't have those instincts that the human race would simply fail to survive. And the first one we talk about is called the social instinct. And he said all human beings are born with the desire to be liked. To be accepted. To be respected by others. To be able to come together in groups with other human beings. And he said if we didn't have that social instinct, we would care nothing about each other. The world would go into the complete anarchy. Dog eat dog would rain and sooner or later under those conditions, the human race would simply fail to survive. So those desires that you and I have. To be a part of. To be recognized by other people. To join together in groups with other human beings, it is a basic God-given thing. It's a good thing. It's necessary for our survival. He uses several words underneath the social instinct. He talks about companionship. That's nothing more than wanting to belong or to be accepted by other people. So many of us grew up on the outside of. The crowd looking at him. Wanting to be a part of and knew that we could not be, even though we desperately wanted to do so. That's one of the reasons we love to drink so well. He uses the word prestige. Prestigious, wanting to be recognized or to be accepted as the leader. Of the group. The world needs leaders. I guess even back in the old caveman days somebody had to say John, get behind that tree with your spare. Mary Jo, get over there with your club and we'll run this sucker through here and we'll jump him and get him. Have something to eat? Somebody has to do that. And most people take one of two directions. Either let me be a part of or let me be the leader of. And any other case is going to be based upon what other people think of us. If they seem to like us and accept us and recognize us, then we can be a part of, or we can be the leader. He talks about self-esteem. Self-esteem is what we think of ourselves. And usually that's either high or low. If other people seem to accept us as a part of the a part of their group, then we feel pretty good about ourselves. But if they reject us, or we even think they reject us, we feel pretty lousy toward ourselves. In either case, it's usually not true. We either think too little or too much. He talked about pride. I'm glad I got in the habit of going. To the dictionary. As a kid growing up, all I ever wanted to be. Was a man who walked tall with pride and a little bit sideway, like John Wayne did. But when I went to the dictionary, I looked it up and I found that I'm not necessarily

don't want to deal with this pride thing. Because the dictionary defines it as an excessive and unjustified opinion of oneself. We either think too well of ourselves or we think too low of ourselves. One of the two. Personal relationships. That's nothing more than our relations with other human beings in the world around us. Ambitions our plans to gain acceptance, power, recognition, prestige and etcetera revolves around our plans for the future. Now if I wanted to be like and accepted and respected by other people. Well, first thing I've got to find out is, well, what do they expect from me? What do I need to become? Society teaches us those things as we grow up and we reach adulthood. In some parts of the world you need. A good education. To be liked and accepted and respected, another part of the world, perhaps, is to be a large landowner. Another part of the world is to be. A good fisherman. And not to the part of the world. It's to be a good farmer. It can be any number of different things. And we're told they were saying about society as. We grow up. And based on what we're taught, then we set goals for ourselves. To get the education to be the landowner to be whatever it is that we decide, we need to be. Now, if you're going. To reach the goal. And be accepted and recognized by other people. You're going to have. To work at it. You can't just be a bum and sit on your Duff and have people like you and accept you and respect you. By the same token, you're probably going to have to make some sacrifices. You know, there are some things that I would really like to do as a human being that are very exciting and very pleasurable, but if I do them and you catch me at it, you're not. Going to like me at all. And I don't think you and I would do the work necessary, nor make the sacrifices necessary unless we got some reward for doing so. The great reward comes at the moment of successful completion of the gold Bill, said it in his story when he said I had arrived. How many of us have set that goal and literally worked our tail off for years to get there? We become successful and they pat us on the back and they. Say oh Joe. You're a good man. You're a smart individual. You're really a great guy and there becomes a feeling on verse. That's one of those indescribably wonderful feelings when we get that recognition. The only thing wrong? With it, though, it seems to. Be just a temporary feeling. Hell, you no sooner get the recognition you feel good over it and you look around you say well. Is this all there is to it? And we set another go and we work and we work and we strive and we strive and we reach the new goal, we get the recognition. It feels good, doesn't last long and we set. Another goal? And it seems to create within we human beings, an insatiable desire for more and more power, more and more recognition, more and more and more. And they're not giving it to us fast enough. We're not getting it the way we think. We ought to get it. So what do we do? Well, we start taking shortcuts. We start doing little lying and little conning. A little manipulating a little, stepping on other people's toes and climbing on their backs, and the instant we do so we create pain and suffering for ours. They in turn retaliate against us and create pain and suffering for us. Explain that life run on self-will can hardly ever. Be a success. Because under those conditions, we're always in collision with people and places and things. He talked about another Basic Instinct. He called it the security instinct. He said all human beings are born with a desire to be secure in the future, he said. If we didn't have that desire. We wouldn't provide the food, the clothing, the shelter, the protection, the things that we have to have in order to survive next winter season. We would just freeze to death. Next drought season, we would simply start to death. Now I know when a we try to live. One day at a time. But I also know everybody in this room has got an insurance policy. And the purpose of an insurance policy is to protect ourselves in the future. A basic God-given instinct. And it's. A good thing? But just like with the with the social instinct, if you're going to be secure in the future. The first thing you have to do is decide what is it I need to be secure. Society teaches us that as we grow up. And one part of the world they need $4. Another part of the world I need 4000. Another part of the world I need 4,000,000. Another part of the world I need a. 190. Two coconuts. Whatever it is they use to measure and trade and border with. And we start setting goals for ourselves. Now, if you're going to reach the goal and be secure in the future, you're. Going to have to. Work at it. You can't just sit on your Duff and be about and be secure in the future. By the same token, we're going to have to. Make some sacrifices. I can't blow it all today on what I want. If I want to be secure in the future. And I don't think we would do the work necessary to make the sacrifices necessary to be secure in the future unless we get a reward for doing so. And the great reward comes at the moment of successful completion. Of the gold. My God, how many of those goals have we set for ourselves as a kid? Growing up, I set the goal for a bicycle. chapters.title: Chapter 86 A Design for Living
chapters.content:
Chapter 86 A Design for Living

Now, way back in the book we talked about. We've been try dimensional creatures. The book said that we are spiritually ill we're mentally ill and we're physically ill and it said when the spiritual malady is overcome. We straighten out mentally and physically. And I think what that's referring to are the three dimensions of life. All human beings are born to live. In three dimensions of life. You know, if God dwells within each of us. And that means we're going to have to live with God, whether we. Like it or not? That's beside the point. The only question is, do we live with God in harmony or disharmony? I don't know of any group of people that ever got in more disharmony with God than we Alcoholics have. We were spiritually ill. We all have a mind. Sometimes we act like we don't, but we do. And we're going to have to live with our mind, whether we like it. Or not specie the point. The only question is, do we live in our minds in harmony? And I don't know of any group of human beings that ever got any sicker in their minds. And we Alcoholics did. We became mentally ill also. The physical dimension I for years thought it was. Just my body. But today I realized the physical dimension is the world and everything in it. My wife, my children, my neighbors, my coworkers, my automobile, my everything in the material world. And we don't have any place else to live here except on Earth. Whether we like it or not, it's beside the point. The only question is, do we live here in harmony or disharmony? I don't know of any group of people who ever got any more disharmony. With the world and everything and everybody in it, and we Alcoholics, did we were sick spiritually, mentally and physically. One day, in reading the big book and this was back in Bill’s story, I read a little segment that said that this is a design for living. That really works. And as we begin to look at these first nine steps. We believe today that they are designed. To put us back together as God intended for us to be in the first place. Three steps, 1-2 and three. We got right with God. Because we were powerless, we saw the. Need for the power. And we made a decision to. Go after that power. And we decided that from hereafter God was going to be the director. He's the father. We're the children. He's the employer. We're the employee, so we begin to develop the proper relationship with God in steps 1-2 and three, and we begin to get right with God. Through four 5-6 and seven, we begin to get right with ourselves. We looked into. Our minds, not other peoples, but in our minds. And we found those things that was created all the problems for us. We talked about them to another human being. We begin to work on their removal in step six and seven, and slowly, slowly, we begin to straighten out in the mental condition we got right with ourselves through steps 456 and seven. Through steps 8:00 and 9:00. We got right in the physical dimension. As we went out and we made our amends to those we've harmed in the past, in our relationship with the world and everybody in it became better and better and better and better and better and better. A design for living. That really works. Under the worst circumstances, there can possibly be. And if you notice, they have to go in sequence. 1-2 and three with God. 456 and seven with ourselves. And in eight and nine with a fellow. Man, I couldn't do it 4-5, six and seven without getting straight with God. I couldn't do 8 and 9 without getting straight with myself. But each one of those removes enough self-will to let me advance to the next stage until I finally get OK with God, with me, and with my fellow man. Now, I don't think it's by accident. At the very next thing we read in the big book, Alcoholics Anonymous. Are called the promises. They are the results. And being straightened up with God, ourselves, and our fellow human beings, and begin at the bottom of that page. 83. Let's look at those for just a few moments.
